newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African Wed money market shortage dips slightly.
newsitem.headline: South African Wed money market shortage dips slightly.

text.p: South Africa's daily money market shortage dipped slightly to 9.677 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.810 billion on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.

But despite the slightly lower shortage, commercial banks lifted their three-month NCD rates to between 16.95 and 17.15 percent from 16.85 and 17.10 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was hiked to 16.35 to 16.50 from 16.25 to 16.45 percent.
Short-term rates are more than discounting a one percentage point increase in the key Bank rate, currently 16 percent.
Money market traders said pressure on liquidity would continue until around the end of January as Christmas spending was likely to exacerbate the situation.
